Source slide page 6 (extracted text):
ENGINEERING CHEMISTRY 
Energy Storage Devices

Electricity Storage density: 
 Amount of charge or electricity per unit weight which the battery can hold
            ESD= Capacity/ Weight of the battery
Weight includes weight of all the components of the battery - electrodes, electrolyte, case, current collectors, terminals etc 
To get high  electricity storage density, use of right kind of material for all the components is important
e.g.,  7g of Li is required at anode to give 1F of charge whereas 104g of Pb is required for the same amount of charge

Source slide page 7 (extracted text):
ENGINEERING CHEMISTRY 
Energy Storage Devices

Cycle life : 
 Number of charge/discharge cycles that are possible before failure occurs
 Applicable only to secondary batteries

 Reasons for limited cycle life: 
 Corrosion at contact points 

 Shedding of active material from the plates

 Shorting between electrodes due to irregular crystal 
  growth and changes in morphology

 Depends on efficiency of electrode reactions

Shelf life: 
 Maximum time for which a battery can be stored without
   loss of performance
 Low shelf life due to self-discharge

Tolerance to service conditions: 
The battery has to be tolerant to different service conditions such as variation in temperature, vibration and shock
